segments: The tenth period.
The Arab kings.
to cast images,
and to make molten figures as in their own country,
and to perform sacrifices and drink-offerings according to their custom.
And while they greatly honored the priests (bikkhus/shaman?),
they also did not despise the ascetics (Buddhists/Kamis?).
And both parties remained among them, each doing his work,
without scorning or despising one another,
unlike the nations that possess the Scriptures and the prophets,
where whoever is present
shames and mocks his fellow,
and judges him an infidel.
Now in this book of the priests which is called the *Nom* (Dharma/Nomos),
together with the pagan fables that are in it,
like those which Saint Gregory the Theologian mentioned,
there are also excellent laws.
Namely:
caution against oppression and injury,
and that one should not repay evil for evil,
but good;
and that no one should kill even a small creature,
such as a louse or a gnat.
Moreover, like Plato, they confess the transmigration of souls from body to body:
and that the spirits of the pure, the righteous, and the doers of good deeds, when they die, migrate into the bodies of kings and nobles;
and those of the wicked and unjust, into the bodies of evil-doers who are tortured, tormented, and killed,
and even into the bodies of irrational beasts, reptiles, and birds.
And these priests,
when meat is brought to them to eat,
ask the one who brought it:
"Did you perhaps kill this animal for our sake,
or did you buy it from the market?" And if he says, "For your sake,"
they do not taste it.
Concerning the cause {OCR?} of the Mongols laying waste to the lands of the Persians and the rest of the places to the west of them.
Since the Mongols had no civilised dwelling,
and were in need of garments and carpets
which were transported to them from the cities,
they were in want.
Genghis
Khan commanded and gave a pledge of peace to merchants,
that they might come to them from everywhere,
and that the road-guards, who are called *Qaraqchis*, should not molest them.
Then three men from the city of Bukhara
prepared splendid vessels, fabrics, and other wares that they knew the Mongols needed,
and loaded up and went to the great camp.
And Genghis
Khan commanded,
and they inspected that which was with them;
